title: Scheduler: workload buckets + mixed prefill/decode queue prioritization (tail-latency guardrails)
author: Sofia Ivanova
description: Motivation: We’ve seen repeated p99/p999 regressions under mixed workloads where long-prefill requests (large prompts / long contexts) can monopolize scheduler attention, increasing queueing time for decode-heavy traffic and causing user-visible tail spikes. This PR introduces explicit workload buckets and updates queue prioritization to keep decode progress stable while preserving throughput. Summary of changes: 1) Workload bucketing: classify each request into a small set of buckets based on (a) estimated prefill tokens, (b) expected decode tokens, (c) whether streaming is enabled, and (d) current KV/cache headroom signal. Buckets are intentionally coarse to avoid churn and cardinality issues: prefill_short, prefill_medium, prefill_long, decode_heavy, and mixed_default (fallback). Classification happens once at admission (with a small correction path when the model’s prompt tokenizer estimate diverges beyond a threshold). 2) Queue structure + prioritization: replace the single global FIFO with a two-lane scheduler (prefill lane + decode lane) plus per-lane bucket queues. Scheduling policy is weighted round-robin with aging: decode lane receives a minimum compute share (floor) to prevent starvation; prefill lane is served opportunistically but is backpressured when decode backlog exceeds a threshold. Within a lane, bucket weights favor short work first (reduce queueing), but aging ensures long-prefill requests make progress. 3) Guardrails: add hard caps to queue depth per lane and per bucket (configurable per hardware profile) and fail-fast admission control in overload conditions with explicit error codes. Also add a “mixed_workload_tail_protect” mode that reduces prefill concurrency when p99 queueing time crosses a runtime threshold. 4) Instrumentation: new metrics and tags to make changes observable and to support perf-canary gating: scheduler_queue_ms (lane + bucket labels), scheduler_admitted_total/scheduler_rejected_total (reason labels), scheduler_lane_share (effective compute share), and scheduler_bucket_age_ms (distribution). 5) Feature flag + rollout: behavior is behind runtime.scheduler.workload_buckets_enabled (default off). On enablement, runtime logs include a one-line summary of active policy parameters (weights, floors, caps) and detected hardware SKU for debugging. Benchmarks (benchmark-lab, internal runs): H100 (SXM): mixed prompt length distribution (p50 128 tok, p95 2k tok, p99 8k tok) @ concurrency 64; streaming on. Baseline p99 end-to-first-token: 920ms; with buckets+prioritization: 710ms (-23%). Tokens/sec: -1.8% (within noise; see notes). p99 decode step latency improved by ~17% due to reduced queueing. L40S: same workload @ concurrency 32. Baseline p99 end-to-first-token: 1450ms; new: 1190ms (-18%). Throughput change: -2.6% (expected due to stricter tail-protect guardrail); stability improved with fewer overload-induced timeouts. Notes: (a) The throughput dip is the intentional trade-off for tail protection; on throughput-optimized workloads (uniform short prompts) policy converges close to baseline. (b) Bucket labels are limited (<=5) to keep metric cardinality safe. (c) This PR does not change kernel selection; it only affects scheduling and admission. Follow-ups: integrate bucket thresholds into the hardware tuning profile pack defaults (ENG-4924) and wire perf-canary gating to block merges when mixed-workload p99 regresses >5% (ENG-4930).

conversation: Noah Patel (review): The overall direction makes sense. Two questions: (1) how do we prevent bucket misclassification when prompt token estimate is wrong by a lot? (2) can we guarantee forward progress for prefill_long under sustained decode-heavy load?

Sofia Ivanova (author): (1) Added a correction path: if observed prefill tokens exceed estimate by >25% and crosses the next threshold, we requeue once into the new bucket (bounded to one move to avoid churn). (2) Yes—aging + per-lane floor. Decode lane has a minimum share, but prefill lane also has a minimum share via aging: any request that exceeds max_age_ms will be promoted within its lane and cannot be indefinitely skipped.
Marcus Reed (review): Bench numbers look good, but I want to see the mixed workload setup captured in-repo and runnable. Also please include p95 queueing time and not just end-to-first-token.

Sofia Ivanova (author): Added tools/benchmark_scenarios/mixed_prefill_decode.yaml and updated the benchmark runner args in docs. Also added p95/p99 scheduler_queue_ms breakdown to the benchmark output summary and referenced it in the PR description.

Sean Gallagher (SRE review): Guardrails: what’s the behavior when queue caps are hit? We need a clear overload signal and a predictable error code for API layer handling. Also, ensure flags are kill-switchable without restart in Hosted.

Sofia Ivanova (author): Queue cap overflow returns AdmissionRejected{reason=queue_full, lane=...} which maps to a 503 (retryable) at the gateway. Added a dedicated metric label for queue_full. For kill-switch: flag is runtime-config reloadable in Hosted; added a note + ensured policy swaps are atomic (lane weights/caps updated together).
Allison Grant (observability): Please keep label sets bounded. lane+bucketing is fine, but do not add model_id here. Also need a single ‘effective_lane_share’ gauge for dashboards.
Sofia Ivanova (author): Confirmed: no model labels. Added scheduler_lane_share (lane label only) and kept bucket labels to the 5 enums. Also added unit test enforcing allowed label values.
Lena Fischer (review): One nit: naming. ‘mixed_workload_tail_protect’ reads like a product feature; can we call it ‘tail_protect_mode’ and document when it triggers?

Sofia Ivanova (author): Renamed to tail_protect_mode and updated runtime config schema + docs. Trigger condition: decode_backlog_ms > threshold OR scheduler_queue_p99 > threshold (whichever first) within a rolling window.
